history.heading: Early peoples
paragraphs: Namibia, in southwestern Africa, has been inhabited for tens of thousands of years by San hunter-gatherers, whose rock art at Twyfelfontein is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Later, Nama, Ovambo, Herero, Damara and other peoples settled the region.

history.heading: German colony and genocide
paragraphs: Germany declared the colony of German South West Africa in 1884. When the Herero and Nama rose up against land seizures, German forces carried out a campaign of extermination from 1904 to 1908, killing tens of thousands, considered the first genocide of the 20th century. Germany acknowledged the genocide in 2021.
South Africa conquered the territory in 1915 and governed it under a League of Nations mandate, later imposing apartheid.

history.heading: Independence
paragraphs: The South West Africa People's Organisation (SWAPO) waged a liberation war from 1966. Under a UN-supervised settlement, Namibia became independent on 21 March 1990, with Sam Nujoma as president. In 2025 Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah became Namibia's first female president.

culture.heading: Diversity
paragraphs: English is the official language, chosen at independence, and Oshiwambo, Afrikaans, German, Herero, Nama and others are widely spoken. The Ovambo are the largest group. Most people are Christian, mainly Lutheran. Himba women are known for covering their skin and hair with red ochre paste.

German influence remains in architecture in Windhoek and Swakopmund, and in food and beer. Namibia is famous for its landscapes: the red dunes of Sossusvlei in the Namib Desert, one of the oldest deserts in the world, and Etosha National Park.

politics.heading: Stable democracy
paragraphs: Namibia is a presidential republic with a stable democracy. SWAPO has governed since independence. Land reform, inequality and unemployment are central political issues. Namibia was the first country to include environmental protection in its constitution.

economy.heading: Mining and beyond
paragraphs: Mining is the backbone of the economy: Namibia is a major producer of diamonds, mostly from the seabed, and one of the largest producers of uranium. Major offshore oil discoveries since 2022 could transform the economy, and Namibia is developing green hydrogen.
Tourism, fishing and cattle ranching are also important. Namibia has one of the highest levels of income inequality in the world. The Namibian dollar is pegged to the South African rand.
